div.div:
Why the strip is built from INPUTS, not from rendered output
1. It works before the first render. A grade or a bubble has to be authored
before it is baked; on an output feed there was nothing to look at.
2. Rendering does not change the view. Edits preview against the input, so
the render bakes what was on screen. On the old feed the render baked the
grade into the output and the preview then graded it a second time.
3. The unit of work is the PAGE — the unit a grade's per-page exclusions and
an overlay's page anchor both address. An output slice can straddle two
pages, so on that feed neither could be honoured at display time at all.

switch.text: Why the strip is built from INPUTS, not from rendered output...

div.div:
Why decodePageToRgba returns the page UNGRADED
Its consumer re-grades on every slider move, and re-decoding a page for
that would cost roughly 100x what grading the buffer costs. The colour
step never influences how a page is READ, so a page fetched once stays a
valid baseline for every grade the user tries on it — which is also why
the call takes no colour argument at all.
The grade engine is the render's own (ColourCorrector), so the preview is
not an approximation of the committed result.

switch.text: Why decodePageToRgba returns the page UNGRADED...

div.div:
Slices are deliberately absent
Slices are a publishing artifact — files to upload. A viewer draws a
continuous strip and hides the seams anyway. What the author still needs
is the slice GRID, drawn as seam guides every sliceHeight down the strip:
the line a bubble must not be split by.

div.div:
Why the ungraded page is kept
The grade is a derived copy, never applied to the resident page.
That is what makes a page fetched once a valid baseline for every
grade the user tries on it — a slider drag re-grades from the same
cached pixels instead of paying ~100x to decode again.
The per-page exclusion is honoured HERE, at display time, by the
same rule the render applies. It is also why the preview's unit of
work is the page: an output slice can straddle an excluded and an
included page, so on a slice feed the exclusion could not be
honoured at all.

switch.text: Why the ungraded page is kept...
